conclusions: H1 confirmed: with a stated day count both models decide elapsed-day rules almost perfectly (4B 0.65 -> 1.00, 9B 0.75 -> 0.975; 14 and 9 paired flips to correct, 0 flips to wrong). The models already consume day counts; the compositional training generator never states one, and the serving preprocessor (KEV_DATE_FACTS) supplies them. Training on day-count renderings would not change the plain case, because the missing capability is the subtraction itself.

H2 not supported at scale: 9B mismatch_decoy_role 0.967 vs mismatch_clean 0.967; decoy_pair 1.000. The 0/6 on transfer-v4 development came from two generated groups. 4B shows a small effect (0.917 vs 0.975, 9 of 10 errors answer accept), worth at most ~1 pp on rule tasks; not a priority for data generation.

Neither hypothesis motivates a training run under the current budget; the elapsed finding is a serving-default decision, and PAWS-style natural role binding has no permitted programmatic training source (would need human labels).
